title: Issue 1 Cover — Between the Beacons
summary: Founding cover for Rex Fleet Academy: Between the Beacons. Sell the Academy as a place where difficult science becomes visible and transferable: Jia Morgan leads a hands-on reciprocal-field demonstration while cadets actively manipulate a ship model and watch an apparently impossible result emerge. The emotional promise is not infrastructure alone but the moment understanding passes from expert to student. Use the issue's corridor physics as the demonstration subject without explaining the full lesson or revealing later route-market, Shard, duty-watch, or Mirrorfold turns.
settingText: Fleet Academy reciprocal-field lecture theater configured as a working engineering demonstration rather than a podium lecture. A large transparent volumetric test apparatus occupies the center of the room: a suspended scale ship model sits inside a measurable reciprocal-field visualization with paired opposing curvature traces, a narrowing central gap, and a soft three-dimensional green safe-volume solution around the surveyed spine. Jia Morgan works beside the apparatus while Nia Voss actively adjusts a navigation/field control; Tomas Reed studies the physical instrumentation and Elian Kade reads the larger route model. Tiered Academy architecture, blue/white/gold institutional materials, real controls, instrument rails, and restrained projection surfaces make the scene feel like an advanced university physics or engineering laboratory. The demonstration is the spectacle.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed vertical comic cover. No interior panel grid, collage, cast lineup, dossier framing, or textbook infographic page.

ONE-SECOND SELLING IMAGE: a future engineering class has made impossible physics visible. The dominant shape is the large reciprocal-field demonstration suspended in the lecture theater, with Jia and the cadets physically engaged around it. The reader should immediately understand that this is a place where people learn how the Rex Fleet universe actually works.

Make the central demonstration visually elegant and physically legible: two reciprocal curvature traces oppose one another around a suspended ship model, the gap between them visibly narrows through the apparatus, and a soft green three-dimensional safe-volume solution resolves around a surveyed spine. Do not turn the display into a magical portal, hard tunnel, or decorative energy sphere.

Jia is the instructor but not a podium lecturer. Stage her beside the apparatus, one hand indicating the relationship between the opposing curves or the narrowing gap while she watches the students' result. Her body language should read as precise, patient and expectant—the expert making room for the student to see it.

Nia is the active learner and strongest human secondary focal point. Put her at the control surface making the adjustment that causes the relationship to become visible. Her expression should be the instant of recognition, not passive awe.

Tomas should be checking the actual hardware response—instrument rail, phase trace, load indication, or mechanical control—so the cover reads as engineering as well as abstract physics. Elian should be connecting the local demonstration to the larger corridor model in the room. Their roles should be readable without posing all four characters toward the camera.

The classroom must feel like a serious college science/engineering environment: apparatus first, active manipulation, close observation, students learning by doing, and enough institutional detail to feel used rather than ceremonial. Avoid giant lecture-hall emptiness and avoid a professor performing at seated rows.

The infrastructure of the wider world may appear only as a secondary contextual projection beyond the apparatus: a restrained green beacon-to-beacon route or civilian traffic model that shows what this physics is for. It must not become the cover's primary spectacle.

OPTIONAL EXACT SCIENCE NOTATION: if mathematical notation is rendered legibly as part of the demonstration, limit it to the canonical relationships k₊(x)=1/x, k₋(x)=−1/x, and g(x)=2/x. Do not invent additional equations, labels, units, pseudo-science text, or dense HUD clutter. If the exact notation cannot be rendered cleanly, use unlabeled curves rather than corrupted math.

Do not show Shard craft, a red public-beacon crisis, private route brokers, leaked BHA diagnostics, the medical-convoy duty-watch problem, the final green-restoration solution, or Mirrorfold geometry. This cover sells the pleasure and consequence of learning the foundational physics before the issue expands into certification, commerce and power.

THUMBNAIL TEST: the apparatus and the human teaching relationship must survive reduction. At small size, the image should still read as instructor + students + one extraordinary experiment, not as four tiny people lost in a room or as an abstract glowing diagram.

TRADE-DRESS ZONE: preserve a clean upper band integrated into the architecture and dark projection field, roughly the top quarter of the cover, with sufficient contrast for the masthead. Do not let the brightest curves or character heads collide with the lettering.

Founding masthead architecture should visibly belong to the released Rex Fleet family: large premium ivory/Ion-White block lettering with restrained gold edge/detail, STAR SPLITTER VISIONS publisher lockup at upper left, ISSUE #1 at upper right, REX FLEET as the parent brand, ACADEMY as the clear sub-brand, and BETWEEN THE BEACONS as the strong topic title. Do not copy the released Rex Fleet Issue 1 character montage or faction-wedge composition.

Color hierarchy: mature Academy blue/white/gold environment; green reserved for the verified corridor/safe-volume result; neutral Ion White instrument light; restrained amber/yellow hardware accents where physically justified. Purple survey and other later color-grammar elements are not needed on this cover. Avoid generic cyberpunk neon, AI beige, magical rainbow refraction, or dramatic red threat lighting.

directionInline.text: This is a single-image prestige science-fiction comic COVER, not an interior sequential page. Do not create a panel grid.

The cover's governing idea is TRANSFER OF KNOWLEDGE. The scientific demonstration and the relationship between instructor and active learners are more important than external infrastructure spectacle. The cover should feel like an exceptional college physics/engineering demonstration in a mature future institution.

Required cover lettering is limited to STAR SPLITTER VISIONS / REX FLEET / ACADEMY / BETWEEN THE BEACONS / ISSUE #1, plus only the optional exact canonical mathematical notation explicitly permitted in the panel plan. No tagline, blurb, character label, fake review quote, environmental signage, route label, pseudo-science filler, or invented HUD text.

Before generating this founding cover, retrieve and visually inspect the actual released Rex Fleet Issue 1 cover pixels from StarSplitterVisions at sites/visions/public/images/covers/rex-fleet-issue-01-green-corridor.jpg. Use those pixels only as parent-family guidance for premium Rex Fleet masthead weight, ivory/gold/black brand language, publisher-lockup placement logic, issue-number prominence, and overall cover finish. Do not copy its character montage, faction wedges, composition, story imagery, or exact palette distribution.

The reciprocal-field demonstration must preserve the technical concept: opposing reciprocal curvature relationships, a narrowing gap, and a ship maintaining a workable dynamic relationship rather than being fired through a tunnel. The corridor/safe-volume visualization remains three-dimensional with a soft physical edge around a surveyed spine.

Do not make Jia the sole spectacle. The student action and reaction must show knowledge being acquired. At least one cadet should be physically operating the demonstration while Jia guides rather than performs.
Judge the art at thumbnail size before accepting it. The cover must still read as 'future engineering students learning impossible physics through one beautiful experiment' when small.

FOUNDING TRADE-DRESS COVER: after this exact cover is approved, persist the approved pixels to production/references/rex-fleet-academy-between-beacons/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.png and activate that asset in production/references/rex-fleet-academy-between-beacons/cover-production-normalization.json. Any later cover for this series must pixel-read that approved asset for masthead/trade-dress continuity before generation.

The approved Issue 1 cover controls later masthead identity, title hierarchy, issue-number treatment, margins, logo scale, and trade-dress geometry only. It must never force later issue-specific demonstration, cast, palette, lighting, camera angle, or story imagery.

source: Between the Beacons founding cover design pass; revised to Academy transfer-of-knowledge / engineering-demonstration cover doctrine, 2026-09-30.
